title: A Passage for the Wreck
premise: Kestrel Lockridge, a railroad engineer who survives by mapping abandoned lines and never sleeping twice in the same town, is drawn to a tide-revealed cave that local legend says grants passage through the mountains—for a price. Inside, Kestrel finds not treasure but a stranded crew of misfits: a disgraced surveyor, a runaway telegraph girl, and an old brakeman who once rode Kestrel's father's trains. Hunted by a railway syndicate that wants the cave's lost tunnel sealed and its discoverers silenced, the found family must cross the range ahead of the snows while a monsoon rising from the coast threatens to flood every low pass. In the climax, Kestrel must choose between burning their map—the record of who they were—and using it to lead the syndicate's men into a dead-end collapse. The book ends with the survivors reaching the far valley as the first snow falls, Kestrel finally staying in one place long enough to be known.
about_author: Sebastian Marchetti is the pen name of a former track inspector who spent eleven years walking remote rail corridors across three continents before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about people who live in the margins of maps.

chapters.title: The Man Who Owns No Address
chapters.summary: Kestrel Lockridge arrives in the port town of Saltmere aboard a freight car, cataloging closed rail lines from memory. POV: Kestrel. The beat is restless competence—Kestrel's rules of invisibility established, and the first crack in them: someone at the station seems to recognize their face.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: An extreme low tide exposes the mouth of a sea cave beneath the old cliff line, exactly where legend says the Wreck Passage begins. Kestrel explores alone against their own instincts. POV: Kestrel. The emotional beat is temptation—staying invisible versus the pull of a mystery that could explain their father's disappearance.

chapters.title: Admission Charged
chapters.summary: Inside the cave, Kestrel finds survey marks in their father's handwriting and a rusted handcar on intact track leading inland. They also find they are not alone: a boy, Pip, has been living there. POV: Kestrel. The beat is shock turning into reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: Three Strangers and a Handcar
chapters.summary: Pip leads Kestrel to others sheltering in the cave: Odile Vasseur, a disgraced surveyor, and Amos Brant, an aging brakeman who recognizes Kestrel's surname. POV: Kestrel. The beat is wary assembly—four people with reasons to vanish discovering they've all been drawn to the same passage.

chapters.title: The Syndicate's Letter
chapters.summary: A notice nailed to the cave mouth offers reward for information on 'trespassers,' signed by the Meridian Railway Consolidated. Odile reveals she was fired for finding the same tunnel records. POV: Odile. The beat is fear hardening into resolve; the group realizes the syndicate has been hunting this passage for years.

chapters.title: Timetable for Ghosts
chapters.summary: Kestrel reconstructs their father's route from the cave's survey marks: a disused summit tunnel crossing the range, passable only before snowfall—six weeks at most. POV: Kestrel. The beat is commitment; Kestrel breaks their own rule and agrees to travel with others.

chapters.title: Saltmere Burns Its Lanterns
chapters.summary: Syndicate agents reach Saltmere, questioning locals. The group flees inland by night on the handcar along the abandoned coastal spur. POV: Pip. The beat is flight laced with exhilaration—Pip's first time belonging to something moving.

chapters.title: The Bridge That Remembers
chapters.summary: A decayed trestle over the Vell River forces a choice: repair it or detour through syndicate territory. Amos's old brakeman skills save the crossing, but he takes a bad fall. POV: Amos. The beat is cost—the first price of survival paid in flesh.

chapters.title: Monsoon Weather
chapters.summary: Coastal radio chatter (a stolen receiver) reports an early, violent monsoon forming offshore. Rain reaches the foothills days ahead of schedule. POV: Odile. The beat is dread arithmetic—every flooded pass eliminates one route, and the clock accelerates.

chapters.title: Company of Liars
chapters.summary: Sheltering from rain, the group exchanges truths: Odile's falsified report, Amos's role in the accident that ended Kestrel's father's career, Pip's real name. POV: Kestrel. The beat is rupture—Kestrel learns Amos was there the night their father vanished, and trust fractures.

chapters.title: The Switch at Hollow Fork
chapters.summary: Kestrel walks out alone rather than forgive, taking the map. A syndicate patrol nearly catches them; only Amos's intervention saves them. POV: Kestrel. The beat is bitter interdependence—you can resent your family and still need them to survive.

chapters.title: Up the Dead Line
chapters.summary: The group climbs the abandoned gradient toward the summit tunnel, handcar abandoned, gear on their backs. Weather turns to sleet. POV: Pip. The beat is endurance—Pip falters and is carried, learning that found family means being carried sometimes.

chapters.title: Snowline
chapters.summary: They reach the tunnel portal as the first true snow falls behind them, sealing retreat. Inside: a collapsed section two miles in, but also evidence someone crossed recently. POV: Odile. The beat is grim hope—the way forward exists, but so does whoever went before.

chapters.title: The Other Party
chapters.summary: They encounter a syndicate survey team trapped by the collapse, led by the agent from Saltmere. Uneasy standoff in the dark. POV: Kestrel. The beat is moral complexity—the enemy is just men following orders, freezing like everyone else.

chapters.title: Terms in the Dark
chapters.summary: Kestrel negotiates: shared labor clearing the collapse in exchange for passage and silence. Odile engineers the shoring; Amos, injured, directs from a stretcher. POV: Odile. The beat is fragile alliance—cooperation under duress, everyone watching everyone.

chapters.title: Water Finds a Way
chapters.summary: The monsoon makes landfall; meltwater and storm runoff begin flooding the tunnel's lower sections. The truce strains as the syndicate men consider seizing the only rope. POV: Amos. The beat is crisis of character—Amos chooses to share the rope, repaying his debt to Kestrel's father.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Rising water forces a sacrifice: the syndicate's youngest agent drowns holding the shoring line, and the survivors escape upward through a ventilation shaft. POV: Kestrel. The beat is grief and guilt—survival is not clean, and Kestrel carries a stranger's death.

chapters.title: Above the Weather
chapters.summary: They emerge onto the high shoulder of the range above the storm, the syndicate remnant scattered or surrendered. One night's rest before the descent. POV: Pip. The beat is stillness—Pip asks Kestrel if they'll all stay together after, and Kestrel cannot answer.

chapters.title: Descent Into the Green
chapters.summary: The far side: monsoon-soaked jungle valleys, washed-out grades, leeches and landslides. The remaining syndicate man, Halloway, becomes a grudging companion rather than a prisoner. POV: Halloway. The beat is transformation—even the hunter is unmoored from what he served.

chapters.title: The Map and the Fire
chapters.summary: Halloway reveals the syndicate will keep hunting unless the original survey records are destroyed. Kestrel must burn their father's map—the last trace of him—to end it. POV: Kestrel. The beat is the book's central choice: identity held in paper versus identity held in people.

chapters.title: Last Light on the Down Grade
chapters.summary: Climax: a final syndicate pursuit party corners them at a river washout. Kestrel uses their intimate knowledge of the dead line to lure the pursuers onto a collapsed culvert, ending the chase without killing anyone. POV: Kestrel. The beat is mastery turned to protection—engineering as an act of care.

chapters.title: A Station Called Home
chapters.summary: Resolution: the five reach the river town of Ferrow's Landing as the monsoon settles in. Kestrel signs the station ledger with a real name for the first time in years and takes work repairing the branch line. POV: Kestrel. The beat is arrival—stopping no longer costs more than staying, because now there is something worth stopping for.
